Perfect. I have enough information now to provide a comprehensive feature inventory. Let me compile this for you.

## GameForge Tab Feature Inventory

**OVERVIEW (dashboard view)**
- Displays: Project hero metrics (entity/rule/note/player counts), game identity (theme, complexity tier, target audience), design stats radar chart (luck/strategy/interaction/complexity/replayability), recent activity timeline, next playtest, open design problems.
- Edits: Game name, elevator pitch, plays-like, age range, complexity tier, theme, mechanic fingerprint scores, overviewMeta fields.
- Key features: Design advisor (AI), project versioning, collaboration dashboard, complexity score widget.
- **Gap**: No quick win calculator, missing "what to design next" prioritization, no AI-driven scope estimation.

**RULES LIBRARY**
- Displays: Categorized rules (movement/combat/economy/turn_structure/variant) with priority dots, designer's notes, edge cases, linked entities.
- Edits: Create/edit/delete rules; drag-to-reorder; categorize by section; set priority; duplicate rules.
- Key features: AI Generate (3 rules at once), AI Enhance (rewrite + design notes + edge cases + related rule suggestions), Conflict Check (semantic LLM analysis), auto-linker (Rule #N references).
- **Gap**: No rule dependency graph, missing "rules that need testing first" flagging, no heat-map of rule complexity.

**ENTITIES**
- Displays: Cards, NPCs, tokens, abilities (12+ types) with stats (parsed from "KEY val / KEY val" format), properties, color-coded by type, status badges (draft/ready/balanced), related-to relationships.
- Edits: Create/edit/delete; add custom properties; bulk-template generation (AI Generate Entities); AI Enhance single entity; manage stats, relationships, color.
- Key features: Grid/list view toggle, type filter, AI enhancement with stat suggestions, property templates by type, relationship mapping.
- **Gap**: No visual stat distribution histogram until Balance tab, no "which entities need playtesting" flag, missing stat-scaling curves (cost vs. power).

**PLAYERS (Actors & Archetypes)**
- Displays: Characters/NPCs/Enemies/Bosses/Creatures/Allies with archetype, role, motivation, strategy, special ability, relationships (allied/enemy/rival), behavior profile (risk/aggression), radar chart per player.
- Edits: Create/edit/delete; drag-to-reorder; set decision style, playstyle tags, resource progression, ability tags, relationships to other players.
- Key features: AI Enhance (write motivation/strategy/flaw), player relationship graph visualization, behavior profile radar, completeness score.
- **Gap**: No interaction matrix (player A's ability breaks player B's strategy), missing "player balance check" (are all archetypes viable?), no turn-order implications.

**NOTES (Design Notes)**
- Displays: Sticky notes (colored: yellow/blue/green/pink) with optional title, pinned status, topic/tag, linked "see also" notes, "look at later" flag counter.
- Edits: Create/edit/delete; pin; flag for later; assign color; tag; link related notes; optional title.
- Key features: AI Enhance (tighten writing), AI Digest (synthesize all notes into pinned summary), sort by pinned + recency, grid layout.
- **Gap**: No search/full-text index, missing note threads/hierarchy (parent-child notes), no "unresolved questions" surfacing from notes.

**TASKS**
- Displays: Kanban (backlog/in_progress/review/blocked/done), table, or calendar view; task title, description, status badge, priority, assignees, due date, tags.
- Edits: Create/edit/delete; bulk status move; bulk delete; select multiple; apply task templates (pre-built checklist sets); filters by assignee, priority, tag, status.
- Key features: Three view modes (kanban/table/calendar), task templates (e.g., "Playtest Prep" with 5 sub-tasks), detail drawer per task, assignee avatars, calendar cell-based task grouping.
- **Gap**: No task dependencies (Task A blocks Task B), missing burndown chart, no task automation (auto-move to "blocked" if rule conflict detected).

**SIMULATOR**
- Displays: Monte Carlo results (health score 0–100, mean final state, bankruptcy rate %), turn-by-turn percentiles (P10/P50/P90), verdict AI summary; AI playthrough transcript (streaming).
- Runs: Monte Carlo (1–10k iterations) over 20 turns; AI Playthrough (dramatized walkthrough with optional focus scenario, streamed line-by-line).
- Key features: Configurable iteration count, streaming playthrough UI, health/bankruptcy risk summary, turn-by-turn trend data.
- **Gap**: No side-by-side scenario comparison, missing "which rule is breaking the game" drill-down, no player interaction distribution (are turns too swingy?).

**BALANCE**
- Displays: AI balance report (balance score 0–100, conflict count, stat dimension count); verdict summary; stat distribution histograms (bar charts per stat showing all entities); Stat Explorer scatter plot (pick X/Y axes from any stat, filter by entity type).
- Key features: AI Report tab (high-level verdict), Stat Explorer (interactive 2D scatter to spot outliers by stat pair).
- **Gap**: No "which rule change would fix this imbalance" suggestion, missing cost-to-power ratio line, no asymmetry check (are all player types equally viable?), stat correlation matrix absent.

**PLAYTESTING**
- Displays: Two tabs—Sessions (date, player count, duration, rating 1–5, positives/issues/suggestions, notes) and Public Feedback (respondent name, date, fun/balance/clarity scores, feedback text); public share link (copyable).
- Logs: New session with player count, duration, 1–5 rating, positives/issues/suggestions/notes; receive public feedback (form on shared link).
- Key features: Public feedback form with numeric scores (fun/balance/clarity), session summaries with sentiment tagging.
- **Gap**: Missing "playtest analysis" (correlation between design changes and next session's score), no feedback tagging/categorization, no "most-mentioned issues" trend, absent session comparison.

---

**Overall Design Gaps from a Working Designer Perspective:**
1. No dependency/blockage system (task blocks rule, rule blocks entity balance check).
2. Missing iteration/feedback loop closures (link playtesting feedback to specific rules/entities for re-test).
3. No "next priority" heuristic (AI recommends what to design/test next based on open problems, rules conflicts, imbalance).
4. Absent drill-down (simulator says game is "broken"—which rule/player/mechanic is the culprit?).
